title: Repairs stall between diagnosis and parts arrival
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Nine-person business PC and laptop repair provider.
owner_narrative: Technicians identify a part, office staff ask suppliers, and customers approve quotes. The gaps between those steps last days. An approval sent to a technician never reached purchasing. Shelves and spreadsheets disagree, and warranty return dates get missed.

diagnostic_interview.question: What is waiting right now?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: The sheet says waiting for parts, but a supplier is actually waiting for a submodel.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Status must expose the next dependency.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: A confirmed manufacturer backorder will not be shortened by reminders; communicate alternatives and expected dates instead.

diagnostic_interview.question: Where does approval arrive?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Email and direct messages, sometimes only to the technician.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Capture approval in the repair record.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Who checks overdue items?
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Are return and loaner obligations tracked?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: They are handwritten on paper labels.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Repair closure is not the only completion condition.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: A simulated approval message predates purchase by four days.
A simulated supplier request lacks the full part number.
A simulated return label has an approaching deadline.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Handoffs lack an accountable next action, complete part identity and explicit deadlines.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: A confirmed manufacturer backorder will not be shortened by reminders; communicate alternatives and expected dates instead.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Assign one repair owner; require exact part verification before purchase; separate waiting for information, approval, supplier and customer.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Track dependency states, deadline reminders and linked loan/return obligations; prepare customer updates from verified status.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: No purchase without applicable approval and verified part identity.
requirements.rationale: Handoffs lack an accountable next action, complete part identity and explicit deadlines.

requirements.statement: A supplier ETA is not a confirmed appointment.
requirements.rationale: Handoffs lack an accountable next action, complete part identity and explicit deadlines.

requirements.statement: Closing repair does not erase an open loaner or return obligation.
requirements.rationale: Handoffs lack an accountable next action, complete part identity and explicit deadlines.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: Direct-message approval becomes a reviewable linked record.
Overdue supplier clarification alerts the responsible person.
A repaired laptop with an outstanding loaner retains that obligation.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Purchasing, loaner and warranty lifecycle extensions are required.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Median and 90th-percentile elapsed repair days, decomposed into active work and dependency waiting.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Assign one repair owner; require exact part verification before purchase; separate waiting for information, approval, supplier and customer. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: A confirmed manufacturer backorder will not be shortened by reminders; communicate alternatives and expected dates instead.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Supplier return policies and alternative-parts approval rules remain unverified.

transfer_rules.applicable_when: Handoffs lack an accountable next action, complete part identity and explicit deadlines.
transfer_rules.do_not_assume: A confirmed manufacturer backorder will not be shortened by reminders; communicate alternatives and expected dates instead.
